# AGENTS.md — opencode-mobile (Iran-friendly fork)

## What this repo is

An Android (and, secondarily, web) client for the [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode)
AI coding agent. Fork of [`dzianisv/opencode-mobile`](https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode-mobile) (MIT),
stripped of every dependency that is unavailable or blocked in Iran: **no Google Play
Services, no Firebase/FCM, no PostHog, no Sentry, no expo-store-review, no third-party push**.

Hard constraint: **do not add** Google Play Services, Firebase, FCM, PostHog, Sentry, or any
third-party analytics/push SDK. Background push is done with the local `bridge/` relay to
**ntfy** (self-hostable). Keep it that way.

## Layout

```
app/                       Expo Router screens ((tabs), session/[id], connection/*)
src/components/            UI (chat/, markdown/, AuthGate, ...)
src/lib/                   sdk.ts (HTTP+SSE client), notifications.ts, storage.ts,
                           usage-limit.ts, i18n/, ...
src/stores/                zustand: sessions, connections, events, settings, auth
bridge/                    notify-bridge.mjs — opencode SSE -> ntfy (dependency-free)
scripts/                   check-version-parity.mjs + the CUA smoke script
.github/workflows/         build.yml (APK + web), security-scan.yml (gitleaks)
```

`android/` and `ios/` are **generated by `expo prebuild`** and are gitignored — do not commit them.

## Key patterns

- **SSE is the source of truth.** `events.ts` connects to `GET /global/event` and dispatches to
  the other stores. `sendMessage` is fire-and-forget; UI updates arrive via SSE.
- **Storage** goes through `src/lib/storage.ts` (keystore on native, localStorage on web).
  New persisted keys must be added to `ALLOWED_PERSISTED_KEYS` in
  `src/lib/persisted-keys.test.ts` with a note. Never persist model/tool output.
- **Notifications** are categorized in `src/lib/notifications.ts`; `usage-limit.ts` classifies
  rate/quota errors so they route to the `limits` category (in-app) and the bridge.
- **No Sentry/PostHog:** `sentry.ts` and `analytics.ts` are local no-op shims kept for
  call-site compatibility.

## Conventions

- Prefer `const`; early returns over `else`; avoid `try/catch` where possible; avoid `any`.
- Tests are `node:test` files (`*.test.ts` in `src/`, `*.test.mjs` in `scripts/` and `bridge/`).
- Keep comments explaining *why*, not *what*.

## Running & testing

```bash
npm install
npm test          # Node 22.17+, uses --experimental-strip-types
npm run typecheck
npm run check:versions
npm run export:web        # static SPA build -> dist/ (served from a trusted origin)
npm run bridge            # relay opencode events to ntfy (see bridge/README.md)
```

Local Android build: `npx expo prebuild --platform android && npx expo run:android`.
**Do not install the Android SDK on a system disk** if you can avoid it; point
`ANDROID_HOME`/`GRADLE_USER_HOME` at an external disk. From Iran, add a Maven mirror for
`google()`/`mavenCentral()`.

## CI

`build.yml` runs on push/PR to `main` and on `v*` tags:
- `test` — version check, typecheck, unit tests
- `build` — `expo prebuild --clean` + `./gradlew assembleRelease`, uploads `app-release` (APK)
- `web` — `expo export --platform web`, uploads `web-dist`
- `release` — on a `v*` tag, attaches the APK to a GitHub Release

The APK is the primary deliverable and is sideloaded (see README). If a Gradle build fails,
the error is published as a check-run annotation (readable without authenticated log access).

# CLAUDE.md

See [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the architecture, the hard no-third-party-SaaS constraint, and the
test/build commands. Project skills live in [`.claude/skills/`](.claude/skills/).

# Connect the phone to an opencode server

## 1. Start the server (laptop / VPS)

```bash
npm install -g opencode-ai
OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=yourpassword opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096
```

## 2. Reach it from the phone

- **LAN:** `http://<machine-LAN-IP>:4096`.
- **Remote (recommended for Iran):** a self-hosted WireGuard tunnel, then
  `http://<wg-server-ip>:4096`. Avoid Tailscale if reliability matters — its coordination
  servers can be slow/blocked.
- **Do not** expose port 4096 to the public internet without a tunnel.

Add the connection in the app: *Add Connection* → URL + `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` → Connect.

## 3. Background notifications (no Firebase)

```bash
# self-hosted ntfy (or use ntfy.sh)
npm run bridge -- --opencode http://127.0.0.1:4096 --ntfy-url https://ntfy.example.com --topic my-opencode
```

Subscribe to that topic with the F-Droid `ntfy` app. The relay maps opencode SSE events
(permissions, questions, completions, errors, rate/quota limits) to ntfy messages, so alerts
arrive with the app closed.

## 4. Verify

- In-app: send a prompt and confirm a streaming reply (proves HTTP+SSE).
- Background: stop the app, trigger a permission request, confirm the ntfy notification.
- `npm run bridge -- --once` does a single dry-run pass if `--ntfy-url ""` is set.

# Ship an Android APK

The APK is built by `.github/workflows/build.yml` on GitHub's runners; nothing is built
locally (no Android SDK required, and Maven/Google mirrors may be blocked in Iran).

## Steps

1. Bump the version in **both** `package.json` and `app.json` (`expo.version` and
   `expo.android.versionCode`). They must match or CI fails.
2. Verify locally:
   ```bash
   npm test
   npm run typecheck
   npm run check:versions
   ```
3. Commit, push to `main` — this produces an `app-release` artifact (the APK).
4. For a tagged release (GitHub Release with the APK attached):
   ```bash
   git tag v0.4.16 && git push origin v0.4.16
   ```

## Notes

- `android/` is generated by `expo prebuild --clean` in CI and is intentionally not
  committed. Never commit it.
- Release signing uses the `KEYSTORE_BASE64` / `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` / `KEY_ALIAS` /
  `KEY_PASSWORD` repo secrets; without them the APK is debug-signed (fine for sideloading).
- If the Gradle step fails, read the check-run annotation — the error is published there
  because workflow logs need authentication.

# OpenCode Mobile — Iran-friendly fork

Control your [`opencode`](https://github.com/sst/opencode) coding agent from your phone —
send prompts, switch model/agent, answer questions, approve permissions, get notified. A fork
of [`dzianisv/opencode-mobile`](https://github.com/dzianisv/opencode-mobile) that works
without any service blocked or unavailable in Iran: **no Google Play Services, no
Firebase/FCM, no PostHog, no Sentry**.

[![Build Android APK](https://github.com/melodiw82/opencode-mobile/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/melodiw82/opencode-mobile/actions/workflows/build.yml)

---

## Why this fork

Upstream is built for the Play Store and ships telemetry to third-party SaaS. From Iran those calls
fail or hang, and the app can't be published — so the client is unusable out of the box. This
fork removes the whole third-party surface and ships as a **self-installed APK built by GitHub
Actions**, so nothing in the app talks to a service you can't reach.

| | Upstream | This fork |
|---|---|---|
| Distribution | Google Play · F-Droid · APK | **Direct APK** from GitHub Actions (sideload) |
| Notifications | Firebase (FCM) | **Self-hosted `ntfy`** + in-app |
| Crash reporting | Sentry | **Removed** — local log buffer only |
| Analytics | PostHog | **Removed** |
| Rate/quota alerts | folded into generic errors | **dedicated “Usage Limits” notification** |
| Credentials | Play/OS keystore | OS keystore (Android) · `localStorage` (web) |
| Targets | Android + iOS | **Android** (primary) + **web SPA** (secondary) |

**The result:** the same capable client, minus everything that breaks in Iran — and one new
notification channel you'll actually want (usage limits).

---

## What it does

- **Chat with the agent** over HTTP + SSE, with streaming replies and diffs
- **Model, agent/mode and variant pickers**, switched per session
- **Permission prompts and questions** answered from the phone
- **Multiple connections** (LAN, WireGuard, Tailscale) side by side
- **Biometric unlock**, OS-keystore credentials, offline demo session
- **Notifications** for permissions, questions, completions, errors, connection loss, and
  **rate/quota limits** — with a built-in Android keep-alive, so they arrive with the app
  backgrounded and no Firebase involved

---

## Install (Android, no Play Store)

1. Open this repo's **Actions** → latest green **Build Android APK** → download the
   `app-release` artifact (`app-release.apk`).
2. Copy it to the phone and install (allow *Install unknown apps* for your file manager).
3. No release keystore configured ⇒ the APK is debug-signed. That is fine for personal
   sideloading; add the `KEYSTORE_BASE64` / `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` / `KEY_ALIAS` /
   `KEY_PASSWORD` repo secrets for a stable release signature.

You do **not** need an Android SDK or an unblocked Maven mirror on the phone side — the APK
is built on GitHub's runners.

---

## How to use it

Three things: run the server, point the phone at it, done.

### 1. Run the server (on your laptop or a VPS)

```bash
npm install -g opencode-ai
OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=pick-a-password opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096
```

That's it — that one command is the backend the phone talks to.

### 2. Point the phone at it

- **Same Wi-Fi (30 seconds):** put `http://<your-laptop-IP>:4096` in the app, log in with the
  password above. Find the IP with `ipconfig` (Windows) or `ip addr` (Linux).
- **Away from home:** install the free [WireGuard](https://www.wireguard.com/install/) app
  (also on F-Droid), run the [wg-easy](https://github.com/wg-easy/wg-easy) Docker image on
  your server, scan the QR code in its web UI once, and use the server's tunnel IP. No
  account, no third party, nothing to configure by hand.

### 3. Use it

*Add Connection* → URL + password → **Connect** → pick a model → chat. Permissions, questions,
model/agent switching and diffs all work from the phone.

---

## Notifications

**Built in by default** — nothing to run. While the app is connected, a quiet foreground
service (Android, no Firebase) keeps the session alive so alerts arrive even with the screen
off or the app in the background. Turn it off in **Settings → Notifications → Keep Connected in
Background**.

| Category | Fires when | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Permission Requests | a tool needs approval | on |
| Questions | the agent asks you something | on |
| Task Completed | a run goes busy → idle | off |
| Errors | a session hits a non-limit error | on |
| **Usage Limits** | rate limited, or a free/usage quota is hit | on |
| Connection | the server is unreachable for a while | on |

**Optional: never miss one while the app is closed.** If the phone kills the app, run the
included relay on the machine that runs opencode — it forwards events to a self-hosted
[`ntfy`](https://ntfy.sh) topic you subscribe to with the F-Droid ntfy app:

```bash
npm run bridge -- --opencode http://127.0.0.1:4096 --ntfy-url https://ntfy.sh --topic my-opencode
```

See [`bridge/README.md`](bridge/README.md) for flags (dry-run, `--once`, auth).

---

## Web build (optional)

```bash
npm run export:web        # -> dist/ (index.html + one JS bundle)
npx serve dist            # serve from an origin you trust
```

Serve it and open it in a browser; it talks to the same server. Add that origin to the server
so the browser is allowed to connect:

```bash
opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096 --cors https://your-web-origin
```

Native-only features (biometrics, the background service) are inert on web; the ntfy relay
still delivers alerts. Credentials live in `localStorage`, so only serve it from a trusted
origin.

---

## Build from source

```bash
npm install
npm test                  # 280 unit tests (Node 22.17+)
npm run typecheck
npm run check:versions
```

Android: `npx expo prebuild --platform android && npx expo run:android`. The `android/`
project is **not committed** — it is regenerated from `app.json` on every build, so a stale
native tree can't break it. **From Iran**, add a Maven mirror that proxies `google()` /
`mavenCentral()` to the generated Gradle files and set `GRADLE_USER_HOME`.

CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) builds the APK and the web bundle on every push to `main`
and on `v*` tags; a tag also attaches the APK to a GitHub Release.

---

## Privacy

Nothing leaves your device and your server except the AI requests your opencode server makes
with your own keys. The app never sees your model API keys. The optional relay runs on your
machine and posts to the ntfy server **you** choose.

---

# notify-bridge

Self-hosted background notifications for the OpenCode mobile client — **no Firebase, no
Google Play Services, no third-party SaaS**.

The app can only show notifications while it is alive. `notify-bridge.mjs` runs on the
machine that hosts your opencode server, tails the server's Server-Sent Events stream
(`GET /global/event`), and republishes the events you care about to an
[ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) server. The ntfy Android app — installable from **F-Droid**, so
it needs no Play account — delivers them even when OpenCode Mobile is backgrounded or
swiped away.

```
opencode server ──SSE──▶ notify-bridge ──HTTP──▶ ntfy ──push──▶ ntfy app (phone)
```

## Requirements

- Node.js 20+ (uses the built-in `fetch`). No npm dependencies.
- An ntfy server: the public `https://ntfy.sh`, or (recommended) your own.
- The `ntfy` Android app: F-Droid (`io.heckel.ntfy`) or an APK.

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. run it in the foreground to try it
OPENCODE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 \
OPENCODE_PASSWORD=yourpassword \
NTFY_URL=https://ntfy.sh \
NTFY_TOPIC=my-opencode-ChooseA-RandomSuffix \
node bridge/notify-bridge.mjs

# 2. in the ntfy app, subscribe to the same topic.
# 3. trigger something in the app (ask the agent for approval) and watch it arrive.
```

Use a **long, random topic name** on a public ntfy server — the topic is the only secret
in the naive setup. For anything sensitive, self-host (below).

### Options

| Flag | Env | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--opencode-url` | `OPENCODE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:4096` | opencode server base URL |
| `--user` | `OPENCODE_USER` | `opencode` | Basic-auth username |
| `--password` | `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` | *(none)* | Basic-auth password |
| `--ntfy-url` | `NTFY_URL` | `https://ntfy.sh` | ntfy base URL; **empty string = dry-run** |
| `--topic` | `NTFY_TOPIC` | *(required)* | ntfy topic to publish to |
| `--token` | `NTFY_TOKEN` | *(none)* | ntfy bearer token (self-hosted auth) |
| `--click` | `NTFY_CLICK` | *(none)* | URL opened when a notification is tapped |
| `--once` | — | off | exit after the first publish (smoke test) |
| `--verbose` | — | off | log every event, not just published ones |

`--ntfy-url ""` makes the bridge print what it *would* send without contacting anything —
handy for testing.

## What gets published

| Event | Title | Priority | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permission.asked` | Approval needed | 4 | shield |
| `question.asked` | the question header | 4 | question |
| `session.error` with a throttle phrase | Rate limited | 4 | hourglass, warning |
| `session.error` with a quota phrase | Usage limit reached | 4 | moneybag, warning |
| `session.error` otherwise | Session error | 4 | x |
| `session.status` busy → idle | Task completed | 3 | white_check_mark |
| `session.status` retry | Rate limited | 3 | hourglass |

Identical events within a 2-minute window are suppressed (`--once` disables that).

## Self-hosted ntfy (recommended)

Running ntfy on the same box as opencode keeps the whole path on your own infrastructure:

```bash
# Docker
docker run -p 8080:80 -v /var/cache/ntfy:/var/cache/ntfy binwiederhier/ntfy \
  serve --cache-file /var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
```

Then point both the bridge and the ntfy app at `http://<host>:8080`, and turn on ntfy's
built-in access control if the server is reachable beyond your LAN/WireGuard:

```bash
NTFY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 NTFY_TOPIC=opencode NTFY_TOKEN=<your-token> \
OPENCODE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 OPENCODE_PASSWORD=yourpassword \
node bridge/notify-bridge.mjs
```

In the ntfy app: **Settings → Manage users → Add → Use another server**, enter
`http://<host>:8080` and the same credentials.

## Running it as a service

**systemd (Linux):** create `/etc/systemd/system/notify-bridge.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=opencode notify-bridge
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Environment=OPENCODE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096
Environment=OPENCODE_PASSWORD=yourpassword
Environment=NTFY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080
Environment=NTFY_TOPIC=opencode
Environment=NTFY_TOKEN=your-token
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/opencode-mobile/bridge/notify-bridge.mjs
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now notify-bridge
```

**Windows:** run it under `pm2` (`pm2 start bridge/notify-bridge.mjs --name notify-bridge`),
or a Task Scheduler job with trigger *At startup* and action `node <repo>\bridge\notify-bridge.mjs`,
setting the env vars in the task.

The bridge reconnects automatically with exponential backoff if the stream drops.

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing arrives.** Run with `--verbose` and confirm events are seen. Then check the
  topic is subscribed in the ntfy app and that `--ntfy-url` is reachable *from the
  bridge host*.
- **HTTP 401/403 from ntfy.** The server has access control; set `NTFY_TOKEN` (bearer) or
  include credentials in `NTFY_URL`.
- **HTTP 401 from opencode.** Set `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` (and `OPENCODE_USER` if you changed
  the default).
- **`--ntfy-url ""` prints but sends nothing.** That is dry-run by design.

## Tests

```bash
node --test bridge/notify-core.test.mjs
```

These cover the event→notification mapping, limit classification, dedupe and SSE framing.

# Contributing

Thanks for helping. This fork keeps a hard constraint: **no Google Play Services, Firebase,
FCM, PostHog, Sentry, or any third-party analytics/push SDK.** PRs that add such a
dependency will be declined. See [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the architecture and patterns.

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/melodiw82/opencode-mobile.git
cd opencode-mobile
npm install
```

Node 22.17+ is required (`npm test` uses `--experimental-strip-types`).

## Checks before you push

```bash
npm test              # unit tests
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
npm run check:versions
```

CI runs the same on every push, plus an Android APK build and a web export.

## Running against a real server

```bash
npm install -g opencode-ai
OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=devpassword opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096
npx expo run:android    # full dev build (Expo Go can't load biometric/secure-store modules)
```

Emulator: `http://10.0.2.2:4096`. Physical device: `http://<your-LAN-IP>:4096`.

## Conventions

- Functional components with typed props; zustand stores in `src/stores/`; HTTP/SSE through
  `src/lib/sdk.ts`; file-based screens via Expo Router under `app/`.
- Prefer `const`, early returns, no `try/catch` where avoidable, no `any`.
- New persisted keys must be added to `ALLOWED_PERSISTED_KEYS` in
  `src/lib/persisted-keys.test.ts`. Never persist model or tool output.

## Pull requests

Fork, branch off `main`, keep commits focused, make sure the checks above pass, then open a PR
against `main`. UI changes should include a screenshot.
